parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the hardcoded ProgressBar and Percentage output, the need to ignore arguments while collecting them with std::env::args, zero external dependencies, Cargo project structure, root test2.rs, and byte-identical verification.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent did brief binary probing, then assigned one subagent to implement and verify the Rust port and one separate subagent to characterize the reference binary; the parent retained final inspection and closure.
parallel.implementation: The implementation child created Cargo.toml with a library and binary target, split library code into src/lib.rs, src/progress_bar.rs, and src/percentage.rs, and made test2.rs use path modules so rustc and Cargo builds both worked.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child wrote directly to /output and the parent later listed /output and compared both produced binaries against the reference, so the delegated implementation was already in the final artifact location.
parallel.verification: The implementation child ran cargo build, rustc, multiple diff checks, and cmp; the QA child independently tested argument, stdin, stderr, and determinism behavior; the parent ran a final cmp on both built binaries.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect task behavior is visible at closure; the official evaluator passed all 40 testcases.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the fixed output, ignored argv while collecting std::env::args, built a Rust 2021 Cargo project in /output, used only std, and targeted byte-for-byte output matching.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent owned probing, implementation, build, verification, and final reporting without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote Cargo.toml, src/indicators.rs containing ProgressBar and Percentage, and root test2.rs using a path module; it used f64 internally for the progress calculation and f32 for Percentage.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were written by the same actor directly under /output, including a rustc-built executable and Cargo release build artifacts copied by the final artifact validator.
serial.verification: The serial agent checked the reference binary with xxd, built with rustc and Cargo, diffed and cmped no-argument output, and ran an additional with-arguments comparison.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect task behavior is visible at closure; the official evaluator passed all 40 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt obligations and additionally confirmed the constant 45-byte output before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt obligations and directly confirmed the same fixed output before writing code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference; both treated argv as ignored and produced the fixed two-line output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work between an implementation child and an independent QA child, while the parent kept final acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, build, verification, and closure in the main agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel decomposition added a QA lane but did not leave implementation, integration, assembly, or end-to-end ownership missing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child received the exact output bytes, module layout, rustc and Cargo requirements, and verification commands; the QA child received a separate read-only behavior-probing brief.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had all task context in one actor and did not require cross-agent interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff boundaries, but the child briefs and returned reports carried the facts the parent needed and produced compatible final work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child wrote a Cargo project with separate progress_bar and percentage modules plus root test2.rs using #[path] module declarations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent wrote a Cargo project with a single src/indicators.rs module and root test2.rs using a path module.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Implementation organization differed, but both implemented the hardcoded output path and argument collection required for the task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both parallel children completed and their combined AgentSwarm result was returned to the parent before the parent performed its final check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated result lifecycle; all information stayed in the main agent until final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join and handoff step absent from serial, but the parent consumed the completed child outputs and no result was trapped or ignored.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the implementation child wrote /output files, while the QA child used /tmp and the parent later inspected the final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent wrote all /output files itself and verified the generated binary outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared final workspace, but no competing writer or overwrite is evidenced; integration was direct because the child wrote the final deliverables.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had child-level Cargo, rustc, diff, and cmp checks, QA behavior probing, and a parent final cmp before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had local xxd probing, rustc and Cargo builds, diff and cmp checks, and an with-arguments comparison before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel performed more distributed verification, while serial performed enough local verification; both satisfied official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout, with two subagents and a longer 219.831 agent-second run, leaving enough budget for parent final checks and closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout in 112.004 agent seconds and closed after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed more tokens and elapsed time due to delegation, but the extra work did not displace implementation, verification, or delivery.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed evaluation records for both modes show solution_passed true with 40 passed of 40 evaluated testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is organizational rather than outcome-relevant: parallel delegated implementation and QA to separate children and then spot-checked their result, while serial did all work in one agent. Both produced byte-identical Rust binaries for the required output.
parallel_contributors: Implementation child produced the final Rust project and verified both Cargo and rustc builds.
QA child independently confirmed the reference binary ignores arguments and stdin.
Parent consumed the child reports and ran a final byte comparison before closure.
serial_contributors: Single agent probed the reference output, implemented the project, built it, and verified no-argument and with-arguments output equality.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used separate progress_bar and percentage modules with f32-oriented arithmetic, while serial used one indicators.rs module with f64 progress fields; neither difference affected the tested output.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparison describes process and structure differences only

candidates.reason: Parallel explicitly assigned the implementation and verification of the Rust port to agent-0, which wrote the final project files and built them.
The delegated implementation wrote the final files directly and the parent inspected the resulting /output tree and binary comparisons, so integration was not unowned.
Agent-0 was told to build both Cargo and rustc outputs and did so, while the parent verified the assembled deliverables before final response.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition by delegating implementation and QA, receiving results, spot-checking artifacts, and closing after successful verification.
The parent's brief xxd probing preceded delegation, but it did not block productive work into an unfinished or shortened closure window.
The parallel run overlapped implementation and QA after the parent probe rather than completing all investigation as a serial first phase that harmed implementation.
No indispensable implementation or verification path was starved; the implementation child completed and parent verification still ran.
The fan-out was only two children, both completed, and the status record shows no timeout or budget exhaustion.
The implementation child had a bounded small porting task and completed it with build and diff evidence, so no oversized unfinished child scope appeared.
The implementation brief included the fixed output bytes, module layout, std-only constraint, root test2.rs, argument collection, build commands, and verification requirements.
Parallel did not assign separately produced components that needed an omitted interoperability contract; only the implementation child wrote final code and QA reported behavior.
No known finding disappeared in transfer; the AgentSwarm result returned both the implementation summary and QA behavior report.
The returned child summaries were long but decision-structured and the parent reduced them to final checks and a concise final answer without leaving dependent work unfinished.
No child result described a superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent then consumed incorrectly.
The implementation and QA reports were compatible: both identified the same constant output and successful byte-identical behavior.
The parent did not accept solely from file existence or component checks; it ran final byte comparisons against both produced binaries before reporting completion.
No replacement or retry child appears in the parallel trajectory; both subagents completed on their first assigned scopes.

candidates.reason: Neither child was cancelled or interrupted; both returned completed summaries to the parent.
A usable implementation existed and was promoted in time; parent final checks completed before closure.
No later child result was merged after verification; implementation verification ran in the child and the parent ran post-handoff verification.
The delegated implementation was already written into /output and the parent inspected and compared the resulting binaries, so the implementation was joined.
The QA child returned its concrete behavior report inside the AgentSwarm result before parent closure.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; there was no unfinished child scope requiring takeover.
The parent explicitly used the completed subagent results, saying both agents finished, then ran its own final spot-check before final response.
The parent did not wait to timeout; it received child results, inspected final artifacts, and the status record reports timed_out false.
There were no competing component designs from concurrent writers; agent-0 owned all /output implementation files and QA did not write implementation files.
No two live agents edited the same source file; only agent-0 wrote source and configuration files under /output.
No source file written or owned by one parallel actor was replaced by another actor.
Only the implementation child wrote test2.rs and test2_bin; no live competing owner overwrote a submitted entry point or executable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final-tree outputs owned by another parallel actor.
The shared /output workspace did not become unstable or lose provenance; there was one implementation writer and parent verification succeeded.
The QA child used /tmp for scratch output and no actor consumed another actor's temporary files or cache as a stable reference.
